# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA**
- Digital Camera World's top pick: 2600 mAh, about 85% charge kept after a year, rated for up to 500 recharges. The reviewer reports years of reliable flash use in harsh conditions.
- Listed prices run roughly $22 to $35 per pack, and the guide links to Adorama, Amazon, Newegg and Best Buy: [Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)
- Best for cameras, flashes, flashlights and game controllers.

**Longest life: Panasonic Eneloop (standard) AA**
- It has lower capacity (2000 mAh) but is rated for up to 2,100 recharges and about 70% charge after 10 years.
- It's best for remotes, clocks and anything you want to set and forget. Buy links are in the same [guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries).

**Best budget: IKEA LADDA**
- Charge-Test measured the LADDA 2450 mAh and 1900 mAh cells at or near their rated capacity, close to the Eneloop Pro and standard Eneloop. It concludes they are Eneloop-class cells at a lower price, though IKEA has never confirmed who makes them: [Charge-Test review](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)
- The only US listing I could confirm is the 1900 mAh 4-pack at $9.99: [IKEA US](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/). I couldn't confirm US stock or price for the 2450 mAh version, so check your local store.

**Best in bulk: Tenergy Premium PRO 2800 mAh (20-pack, $42.99)**
- The seller lists 85% charge after a year and 1,200 cycles: [Tenergy 20-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack)
- Those figures come from the seller, not an independent test. Treat high mAh claims on lesser-known brands with some caution.
- This is an affiliate link.

**Charger: Tenergy TN480U 8-bay ($23.99)**
- It has per-slot LCDs and bad-cell detection, and charges AA or AAA NiMH. It needs a USB power adapter, which isn't included: [Tenergy TN480U](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger) (also an affiliate link).

**If your device needs a true 1.5V:** Digital Camera World recommends the EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA. NiMH cells run at 1.2V, which a few devices read as low. See the [guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) for purchase links.

**My pick:** Eneloop Pro for high-drain gear, and LADDA or standard Eneloop for everyday items. Skip the cheapest high-mAh brands for demanding devices. Another test site (Frame & Focal) found one such brand held up poorly under load, but its figures are inconsistent across articles, so I wouldn't lean on them.
